[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines how enterprise AI agents must access and use evidence sources responsibly, consistently, and predictably. It establishes source classification requirements, permission model assumptions, evidence mapping requirements per intent, and mandatory degraded-mode behavior for when required evidence is unavailable.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all evidence sources used to ground outputs for AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents at Pilot and Production lifecycle states. It does not govern the underlying data access controls of the source systems — those are governed by data governance and security standards. This standard governs the agent's declared relationship to each source and its behavior when sources are unavailable.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. All agents must have a complete Evidence Map before promotion to Pilot state.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

AI agent output quality depends directly on the quality, availability, and appropriateness of the evidence used to ground responses. Without explicit source classification and degraded-mode behavior, agents may silently degrade in quality, make speculative assertions when data is unavailable, or inadvertently use data sources that are inappropriate for the agent's use case or audience.

page_texts.9:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Source Classification:**

Every evidence source used by an agent must be classified as one of:

- **Required** — the agent cannot produce reliable output without this source; absence triggers degraded-mode behavior
- **Optional** — the agent produces better output with this source but can function without it; absence does not trigger degraded mode
- **Prohibited** — this source must not be used by this agent under any circumstances without an approved exception (see Exceptions Process)

Each source must also include:

- Sensitivity classification — the data sensitivity level of the source content
- Data owner — the named individual or team responsible for the source's accuracy and access governance
- Refresh expectations — the expected update cadence for this source's content
- Known limitations — documented constraints or gaps that affect agent output quality when using this source

**Permission and Access Rules:**

- Agents must operate under permission-trimmed assumptions: they must not assume that the user has access to data the user has not been granted access to
- Agent definitions must not assume universal data visibility; role-based output expectations must be documented in the Evidence Map
- Missing-source behavior must be explicitly defined for each Required source

**Evidence Mapping per Intent:**

Each intent defined in the capability contract must map to:

- Minimum required evidence set
- Preferred evidence priority order when multiple sources are available
- Fallback evidence alternatives when preferred sources are unavailable
- Explicit no-evidence response behavior: what the agent outputs when no relevant evidence is retrievable

**Degraded-Mode Behavior:**

When a Required evidence source is unavailable, the agent must:

1. Label the output explicitly as degraded
2. Identify the unavailable source categories (not specific source names if those are sensitive)
3. Limit conclusions to what is supportable from available evidence
4. Avoid speculative assertions that extend beyond available evidence
5. Recommend a next-best-evidence action where applicable
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Document the known limitations of each evidence source so that users can calibrate their reliance on agent outputs when those sources have known gaps
- Prefer permission-trimmed data sources over sources that require agent-level elevated access, to preserve user-level data access expectations
- Define degraded-mode behavior for Optional sources as well, even though degraded mode is only required for Required sources
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Agents must not access sources classified as Prohibited for that agent under any circumstances without an approved exception
- Agents must not produce outputs that assert conclusions derived from a Prohibited source as if that source were permissible
- Agent definitions must not list a source as both Required and Optional for the same intent
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Use of a Prohibited source requires written approval from the Data and Compliance Owner and the Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
2. Exception requests must specify the source, the intent requiring access, the business justification, and the risk controls applied

page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#evidence-map-completeness]

#### Evidence Map Completeness

- The Evidence Map must cover 100% of the intents defined in the capability contract
- Each intent's minimum required evidence set must be specific enough to validate during testing — generic entries such as "project data" do not satisfy the requirement
- Fallback evidence alternatives must be substantive alternatives, not restatements of the primary source
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#degraded-mode-implementation]

#### Degraded-Mode Implementation

- Degraded-mode labeling must appear in the output itself, not only in logs or metadata; users must be able to identify a degraded output from the output content
- The degraded label must identify the category of missing evidence (e.g., "evidence from project tracking system unavailable") without exposing internal source names that are sensitive
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#prohibited-source-enforcement]

#### Prohibited Source Enforcement

- For configured AI agents: prohibited sources must not be connected to the agent's knowledge sources or tool definitions
- For custom AI agents: prohibited sources must be explicitly excluded from the agent's retrieval and tool invocation logic; this exclusion must be documented in the capability contract and verifiable in the code
page_texts.18:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- An agent must not depend on a single Required source with no documented fallback or degraded-mode behavior; single-source dependency without fallback is a design defect
- Permission-trimmed behavior is the default assumption; any deviation from this (e.g., agent identity authentication to a source that provides higher access than the user would have) must be explicitly documented in the Evidence Map and approved by the Data and Compliance Owner

page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#phase-1-evidence-map-authoring-before-pilot]

#### Phase 1: Evidence Map Authoring (Before Pilot)

1. List all data sources the agent accesses or queries
2. Classify each source as Required, Optional, or Prohibited per capability and intent
3. Document sensitivity classification, data owner, refresh expectations, and known limitations for each source
4. Map each intent to its minimum required evidence set, preferred priority order, fallback alternatives, and no-evidence response behavior
page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#phase-2-degraded-mode-implementation-before-pilot]

#### Phase 2: Degraded-Mode Implementation (Before Pilot)

1. Implement degraded-mode labeling for all Required sources
2. Test degraded-mode behavior by simulating each Required source being unavailable
3. Verify that degraded outputs identify missing evidence category and restrict conclusions appropriately
page_texts.23:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#phase-3-ongoing-maintenance]

#### Phase 3: Ongoing Maintenance

1. Review the Evidence Map monthly for source integrity — data owners may change, sources may be deprecated
2. Update the Evidence Map when new intents are added or evidence sources change
3. Review the known limitations field quarterly to reflect any changes in source quality
page_texts.24:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Source classification completeness | All accessed sources classified as Required, Optional, or Prohibited | Evidence Map review | Evidence Map document |
| Per-intent mapping | Every intent has a minimum required evidence set, priority order, fallback, and no-evidence behavior | Capability contract cross-reference | Evidence Map and intent catalog |
| Degraded-mode labeling | Degraded outputs include visible category identification of missing evidence | Scenario testing with sources removed | Test results with degraded-mode scenarios |
| Prohibited source exclusion | No prohibited sources are accessible through the agent | Configuration review (configured agents) or code review (custom agents) | Configuration or code review record |
| Permission-trimmed operation | Agent outputs do not assert data the user does not have access to | Permission profile testing | Test results across multiple user permission profiles |

page_texts.26:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Prohibited source usage detected: immediate containment of the capability
- Degraded-mode behavior undefined for a Required source: block promotion to Pilot
- Unowned source dependency: remediation required before any lifecycle promotion
page_texts.27:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-002-ai-agent-evidence-access.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Data and Compliance Owners (source-level approval); Platform Governance Team (Evidence Map review)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (prohibited source exceptions)
